Tafsir of Surah ʿAbasa (Surah 80)

It is Makkan, and Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾. It is the Messenger (ﷺ) according to all of them. The meaning of ʿabasa is: his face became stern (kalaḥa wajhuhu), and tawallā means: he turned away. The meaning is: he showed disapproval.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿That the blind man came to him﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is "because the blind man came to him," and it is in the accusative as an object. He is ʿAbd Allah ibn Umm Maktum, according to the consensus [of the scholars].

The occasion of revelation of the verse was that the Prophet was speaking with a man from among the nobles of the polytheists, calling him to Islam. ʿAtaʾ said: he was ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa. Qatada said: he was Ubayy ibn Khalaf. Mujahid said: he was ʿUtba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabiʿa, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf. He was calling them to Islam and reciting the Qur'an to them. In some narrations: he had with him a group of the nobles of Quraysh, and he was calling them to Islam, and his eagerness for them had intensified. Then ʿAbd Allah ibn Umm Maktum came and began saying: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me from what Allah has taught you, guide me."

In another narration: he came with his guide, and the Prophet gestured to his guide to hold him back, so he pushed the back of his guide, and the Prophet turned away.

In some narrations from Sufyan al-Thawri: the one who was speaking with him and calling him to Islam was al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib. When Ibn Umm Maktum joined in his address and kept repeating his words, "Teach me, guide me," the Messenger of Allah disliked that until the displeasure appeared in his face, and he frowned and turned away from him. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse rebuking him for what he had done.

In some narrations: that he (peace be upon him) stood up and left.

And His saying: ﴿And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself﴾ — that is, he would purify himself (yatazakka), and the one intended by it is Ibn Umm Maktum.

And His saying: ﴿yuzakka﴾ — that is, he would accept what you remind him of and teach him. It was also said: he would purify himself (yataṭahhar).

And his saying: ﴿or he would take heed﴾ means: or he would be mindful.

And his saying: ﴿so that the reminder would benefit him﴾ means: the reminder and admonition would benefit him.

The meaning is: you turn away from him as one whose instruction and reminder will not benefit him, while you do not know that perhaps instruction and reminder would benefit him; so it is incumbent upon you to teach him and remind him.
And His saying: ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient﴾ — meaning: the one who displays self-sufficiency toward you.

And His saying: ﴿Then you attend to him eagerly﴾, meaning: you expose yourself to him and turn toward him. It is also said that its original form is "tasaddad," and one of the two dāls was changed into a yā'.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 7:

His saying: ﴿And what is it to you if he does not purify himself?﴾ That is, "And what is it to you if he does not become Muslim?" The meaning is that if that person you turned to does not accept Islam, nothing of that falls upon you.
"And His saying: ﴿But as for him who comes to you striving﴾ — meaning: seeking the good."
And His saying: ﴿while he fears﴾, meaning: he fears Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 10:

And His saying: ﴿But you are distracted from him﴾, meaning: you turn away (ta'ruḍ), and it has been said: you occupy yourself with something other than him.

From this is what has been narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "When you see that Allah has given preference to something over you, then leave it alone (falhu ʿanhu), that is: abandon it and turn away from it."

Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna said: "After that, whenever ʿAbd Allah ibn Umm Maktūm came to the Prophet, he would spread out his cloak and say: 'Welcome to the one for whose sake my Lord reproved me.'"

He appointed him as his deputy over Madinah twice, and it has been said several times, when he went out to the ghazw (military campaign).

And in some tafsirs: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was never seen after that reaching out to the wealthy, nor turning away from the poor."

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Never!﴾ Al-Hasan said: "Truly." It was also said: the meaning is that it is for restraint and rebuke, i.e., it is not fitting that the matter be as it has been mentioned before.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a reminder﴾, i.e., this surah is a reminder. It was also said: the reports and stories are a reminder."
"And His saying: ﴿So whoever wills, will remember it﴾ — that is, whoever Allah wills, He inspires him and he remembers it."

In sahf (pages), i.e., the Qur'an; and it is said: the reports and narratives. According to the first view, His saying "so whoever wills may remember it" refers to the Qur'an.

Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfah (a page or scroll).

His saying "exalted" (mukarramah) means: honoured with Allah, and it is said: exalted because it was sent down from a Lord who is Generous.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Raised high﴾ may mean that they are raised high in place, and it may mean that they are raised high in rank and status with Allah, the Exalted.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Purified﴾. Al-Hasan said: purified from every defilement. It was also said: purified, meaning protected from being touched by the hands of the unclean disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 15:

And His saying: ﴿in the hands of scribes﴾. The safarah (scribes) are the angels who convey the revelation (wahy) between Allah and His Messenger. It is also said that the book is called safar, and the mediator who reconciles between a group is called safir. It is derived from making a matter clear and manifest. It is said: "The woman unveiled (safarat) her face" when she uncovered it, and it is said: "The morning shone forth (asfara al-subh)" when it lit up.

From this is the saying of Nawbah ibn Humayr:

﴿When you come to Layla veiled, then indeed her unveiling in the morning has disturbed me.﴾

That is: her appearing (zuhuruha).

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿in the hands of scribes﴾: they are the reciters who recite the verses.

Al-Farra' said regarding His saying ﴿exalted, purified﴾: He called them "exalted and purified" because they were sent down from the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

It was also said: the safarah are angels entrusted with the books (asfar) of Allah the Exalted, and from this comes "the books (asfar) of Musa," whose singular is safar. The poet said:

(So I do not abandon the mediation (sifarah) among my people, and I do not walk with deceit if I walk.)

The intermediary between two parties is called safir because he makes clear what is in the heart of this one and what is in the heart of the other, in order to reconcile them.

And His saying: ﴿Noble, obedient⁠﴾. His saying ﴿noble﴾ is an attribute of the angels, meaning: noble in the sight of God. His saying ﴿obedient﴾ means: obedient ones. It is in the sense of His saying: ﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾. And in some books it is mentioned that in the heaven there are angels who hold the scrolls in their hands, reciting the Qur'an, and their worship is that. This goes back to what we explained earlier, the saying of al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Man is killed; how ungrateful he is!﴾ Then God, may He be exalted, explained, concerning the human being, lessons and signs with which one should not be ungrateful.

As for His saying, ﴿Killed﴾, it means: cursed. "Man" (al-insan) is the disbeliever. It has been said that he is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and it has been said that he is Umayya ibn Khalaf.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas that the verse was revealed concerning Utba ibn Abi Lahab, when God, may He be exalted, sent down the surah "al-Najm." Utba said: "I disbelieve in the star when it sets." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O God, set upon him one of Your dogs." And it is narrated that he said: "O God, set upon him the lion of al-Ghadira" — al-Ghadira being a place. Then he went out afterward in a company of travelers, and when they reached that place, he recalled the Messenger's words. So the people of the company ordered that they guard him that night, and they did so. The lion came, leapt in one bound, got on his back, and tore him apart.

As for His saying, ﴿How ungrateful he is!﴾, it may also be in the sense of reproach. Although the wording is that of a question, the meaning is: What is it that makes him ungrateful to God, when He has shown him of His power what He has shown him?
And His saying: ﴿From what thing did He create him?﴾ Its meaning: Will this disbeliever not reflect on what thing Allah the Exalted created him from? Then He explained what He created him from.

And His saying, ﴿from a drop of semen He created him﴾, and His saying, ﴿then He determined him﴾. Al-Kalbi said: He proportioned his creation, from his two hands, his two feet, his two eyes, and the rest of his limbs, outward and inward. This is in the sense of His saying, ﴿Who created you and proportioned you﴾. It was also said: ﴿then He determined him﴾ means He placed everything in its proper place and prepared for him what would suit him.

Verse 80:20: "Then He made the way easy for him." Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by it is the coming forth from the womb. It was also said that its meaning is: He made the way of good easy for him. And it was said: He made clear to him the way of wretchedness and happiness; this was said by Mujahid, and the one preceding it is the saying of al-Hasan.

And His saying: ﴿Then He causes him to die and assigns him a grave﴾. That is: He made for him a grave in which he is buried. It is said: "qabartu fulanan" means I buried so-and-so, and "aqbartuhu" means I made for him a place in which he would be buried.

Al-A'sha said:

(Had you propped up a dead man against her throat, he would have lived and not been carried to the gravedigger.)

And His saying: ﴿Then, when He wills, He will raise him again﴾ means: He gives him life and resurrects him.

Al-A'sha said:

(Until people say, from what they have seen: "How wondrous, the dead one who rises!")

"And His saying: ﴿Nay, he has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him﴾ means: he has not done what Allah the Exalted commanded him.

Mujahid said: "No one among the creation fulfils all that Allah the Exalted has commanded."

And from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Nay, he has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him﴾, meaning: what He took from him of the covenant on the Day of the Covenant."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 24:

And His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾. That is: let man look at the food and fodder which Allah, may He be exalted, created for the sustenance of creatures. And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that its meaning is: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾, that is, at what comes out of him, how it has changed from the good into the foul.

And it is related from al-Hasan that Allah, may He be exalted, appointed an angel for him, so when a person sits to relieve himself, the angel turns his neck to look at what comes out of him. This was mentioned by al-Naqqash.

He also cited: that Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali asked ʿImran ibn Husayn, "Why does a person look at what comes out of him?" ʿImran did not know what to answer him. Then ʿImran went to Madinah and mentioned that to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and he recited this verse: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾, then said, "He looks in order to know what has become of what he withheld."

Wait, that is incomplete. Here is the full translation:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We poured down the water, pouring [it] down﴾. It was read with a kasra on the alif and with a fatha. So His saying with the kasra, "innā," is in the beginning (ibtidā', a new sentence). And His saying ﴿anā﴾ with the fatha is in the accusative as a substitute (badal) for "al-ṭa'ām" (food), as if he said: "Then let man look at his food: that [anā] We poured down [the water]." This was mentioned by al-Farrā'.

It was also said that its meaning is: "Then let man look at his food, because We poured down [the water]."

And His saying ﴿We poured down the water, pouring [it] down﴾: that is, We caused it to flow in a flowing.
"And His saying: ﴿Then We split the earth, splitting it open﴾, meaning: by the emergence of vegetation."
"And His saying: ﴿So We caused to grow therein grain﴾ — it is wheat and barley, and everything that is the staple food of people."

And His saying: ﴿And grapes﴾ is the well-known grape (ʿinab).

And His saying: ﴿And fodder-herbs﴾ is al-qatt in the dialect of the people of Makkah. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is al-ratbah (green fodder), and this is a well-known statement. It was named qadb because it is cut (yuqdab, i.e. cut off) and then grows again, and it is cut and grows again in this manner.

And olives and palm trees, and dense gardens (ghulban).

And His saying: ﴿And olives﴾: this is the well-known olive.

And His saying: ﴿And palm trees and gardens, dense (ghulban)﴾: the ḥadīqa (garden) is every enclosed orchard that is walled around, and that which is not walled around is not a ḥadīqa.

And His saying: ﴿ghulban﴾, i.e., thick of necks (ghilāẓ al-a'nāq). It is said: "a rajul aghlab" when he is strong and thick-necked.

And it is said: "ghulban" means intertwined, i.e., some of them have entered into others.

And it is said: "ghulban" means intertwined, i.e., some of them have entered into others.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 31:

Wa-qawluhu: ﴿wa-fakihatan wa-abban﴾ (and fruit and pasture). Al-fakihah (fruit) is the thimar (fruits), and al-abb is al-kala' (herbage, grass).

Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: al-abb is the pasture of the livestock (an'am). It was also said: al-abb for beasts is in the position of al-fakihah for people.

Al-Dahhak said: al-abb is the fig (tin). It is narrated from al-Hasan that al-fakihah is whatever of fruits is pleasant and sweet to one.

It is well known that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, recited the words of the Most High: ﴿and fruit and pasture﴾, then said: "We have known the fruit, so what is the abb?" Then he said: "O son of al-Khattab, this, by Allah, is surely (al-takalluf, excessive affectation)," and he threw the staff from his hand.
His words: ﴿A provision for you and for your cattle﴾, meaning: a benefit for you and for your cattle.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 33:

And His words: ﴿Then when the Ṣākhkha comes﴾. Ṣākhkha is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. Ibn ʿAbbās mentioned it, like al-Ṭāmma (the Overwhelming), al-Ḥāqqa (the Inevitable), al-Qāriʿa (the Striking), and similar names. It is also said: the Ṣākhkha is the calamity that creatures are unable to withstand. It is also said: the Ṣākhkha is the Ṣāakka (the one that strikes). It is said: "ṣakhkha fulānan" when he struck him (ṣakkahu).

The poet said:

(O my neighbour, will you not wrestle with me, a wrestling like the striking of stones against boulders?)

That is, like the striking (ṣakk). It is also said: the Ṣākhkha is the Blast of Isrāfīl that strikes the ears. And from some of them: the Ṣākhkha is that to which everything gives ear, that is, listens attentively. It is said: "a man aṣakh", that is, deaf.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 80, verse 34–36:

And His saying: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his companion and his children﴾ — he flees from them because he is unable to benefit them or to be benefited by them.

It is said: he flees from them lest they see the humiliation that descends upon him. And it is said: he flees from them in distress at the magnitude of what he is in. In some tafsirs it is related that His saying ﴿from his brother﴾ refers to Qabil (Cain) fleeing from Habil (Abel).

And His saying ﴿and his mother﴾ refers to the Messenger (ﷺ) fleeing from his mother.

And His saying ﴿and his father﴾ refers to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) fleeing from his father.

And His saying ﴿and his companion﴾ refers to Lut (peace be upon him) fleeing from his wife.

And His saying ﴿and his children﴾ refers to Adam (peace be upon him) fleeing from his wicked children. And it is said: it refers to Nuh (peace be upon him) fleeing from his son.

And His saying: ﴿Every man of them that day will have a matter that occupies him﴾. That is: a concern that suffices him and preoccupies him. Al-Qutaybi said: a concern that diverts him from others. And shan (matter) is a great affair; it is said: "So-and-so is in a shan," meaning he is in a great matter.

It was recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading as "yu'nihi," from ʿanā, yaʿnī, with the ʿayn unpointed (i.e., without a dot-marked letter).

Almost identical: translate faithfully.

Divine words: "Faces that day will be radiant" (Qur'an 80:38). The passage: "His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant﴾ — meaning: joyful, rejoicing [faces]. It is also said: bright. It is also said: it has the sense of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the day when faces will turn white﴾ — meaning: faces that day will turn white."

Final translation:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that day will be radiant﴾, meaning: joyful, rejoicing [faces]. It was also said: bright. It was also said: it carries the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the day when faces will turn white﴾, meaning: faces that day will turn white.
And His saying: ﴿Laughing, rejoicing﴾, that is, from joy and gladness.
And His saying: ﴿And faces that Day will be upon them dust-colored﴾, meaning: gloom and blackness.

And His saying, ﴿Darkness will cover them﴾, meaning: sorrow and grief will overwhelm them. It is also said that it has the same meaning as His saying, ﴿and faces will be darkened﴾. From Ata al-Khurasani: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright﴾, because of how much they were covered with dust in this world for the sake of the truth.

And His saying, ﴿And other faces that Day will be dust-covered﴾, because of how much they laughed in falsehood.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked.﴾ That is, the people of those faces are those who disbelieved in Allah and committed wickedness (fujur), and Allah knows best.
